title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Provisions on the Implementation of the Integrity Code and the Prevention of Conflicts of Interest by the People's Courts
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Provisions on the Implementation of the Integrity Code to Prevent Conflicts of Interest by the People's Courts

Fa Fa [2012] No. 6

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Several Provisions on the Implementation of the Integrity Code to Prevent Conflicts of Interest by the People's Courts are hereby issued to you for earnest implementation.

February 27, 2012

Several Provisions on the Implementation of the Integrity Code to Prevent Conflicts of Interest by the People's Courts

Article 1. These Provisions are formulated to further standardize the conduct of personnel of the people's courts and to promote their integrity, fairness, and law-abiding enforcement, in accordance with the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China and with reference to the Several Rules on Integrity in Government for Leading Cadres of the Communist Party of China.

Article 2. Personnel of the people's courts shall not accept gifts of money, gifts, banquets, or arrangements for activities such as travel, fitness, and entertainment that may affect the impartial performance of their official duties.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 59 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 3. Personnel of the people's courts shall not engage in the following profit-making activities:

(1) Operating commercial or other enterprises solely or jointly with others, or through joint stock participation;
(2) Investing in an enterprise as an investor using another person's name;
(3) Engaging in business activities by means of contracting, leasing, or being employed;
(4) Owning shares or securities of non-listed companies (enterprises) in violation of regulations;
(5) Registering a company or making equity investments within or outside the country (border) solely or jointly with others;
(6) Engaging in private lending activities for profit purposes in their own name or in the name of others;
(7) Engaging in other profit-making activities under their own name or in the name of others that may conflict with the public interest.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 63 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 4. Personnel of the people's courts shall not provide guarantees for the economic activities of others.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 65 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 5. Personnel of the people's courts shall not use their authority and influence of their positions to buy or sell stocks or warrants; they shall not use inside information obtained during case handling work to directly or indirectly buy or sell stocks and securities investment funds, or to advise others to buy or sell stocks and securities investment funds.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 63 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 6. When personnel of the people's courts are adjudicating relevant cases, if they hold, in their own name or in the name of others, shares of listed companies related to the case being adjudicated, they shall voluntarily apply for withdrawal.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 30 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 7. Personnel of the people's courts shall not hold concurrent positions in law firms, intermediary agencies, or other economic entities or social organizations in violation of regulations, and shall not engage in paid intermediary activities such as providing information, introducing business, or offering consultancies to case parties or other market entities in violation of regulations. Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 63 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 8. Within the prescribed time limit after resignation or retirement, personnel of the people's courts shall not engage in the following acts:

(1) Accepting appointments from enterprises, law firms, or intermediary agencies related to cases they originally handled or other business;
(2) Serving as litigation representatives or defenders in cases handled by the court where they originally worked;
(3) Acting as litigation representatives or defenders in their capacity as lawyers.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Articles 17, 30, and 63 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts, respectively.

Article 9. Personnel of the people's courts shall not use their authority and influence of their positions to direct others to promote the appointment of their spouses, children, children's spouses, or other persons with whom they have a special relationship.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 71 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 10. Personnel of the people's courts shall not use their authority and influence of their positions to pay or reimburse expenses for study, training, travel, etc., for their spouses, children, children's spouses, or other persons with whom they have a special relationship.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Articles 55, 59, and 64 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts, respectively.

Article 11. Personnel of the people's courts shall not use their authority and influence of their positions to solicit financial assistance from others or have others pay or reimburse the expenses mentioned above for the purpose of their spouses, children, children's spouses, or other persons with whom they have a special relationship to settle abroad (border), study abroad, or visit relatives.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Articles 56 and 64 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts, respectively.

Article 12. Personnel of the people's courts shall not use their authority and influence of their positions to obstruct relevant authorities from investigating and handling cases involving their spouses, children, children's spouses, or other persons with whom they have a special relationship.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 97 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 13. Personnel of the people's courts shall not use their authority and influence of their positions to engage in the following activities:

(1) Permitting their spouses, children, children's spouses, or other persons with whom they have a special relationship to accept property from case parties and their relatives, agents, defenders, personnel of enforcement intermediary agencies, or other related persons;
(2) Providing convenience for their spouses, children, children's spouses, or other persons with whom they have a special relationship to engage in commercial activities or operate businesses;
(3) Permitting their spouses, children, children's spouses, or other persons with whom they have a special relationship to seek personal gain in their names.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Articles 56, 63, and 64 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts, respectively.

Article 14. Leading cadres of the people's courts and judges serving in adjudication and enforcement positions shall not, in violation of regulations, permit their spouses or children to operate law firms within their jurisdiction or provide litigation representation or other paid legal services to case parties.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 65 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 15. Leading cadres of the people's courts and personnel in comprehensive administrative positions shall not permit their spouses or children to engage in activities within their authority and business scope such as commercial operations, business ventures, or paid intermediary services that may conflict with the public interest.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 65 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 16. Personnel of the people's courts shall not, in violation of regulations, intervene or meddle in market economic activities to accept property or seek benefits for their spouses, children, children's spouses, or other persons with whom they have a special relationship.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Articles 56 and 64 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts, respectively.

Article 17. Personnel of the people's courts shall not, in violation of regulations, interfere with or obstruct relevant authorities from conducting normal supervision and case investigation of market economic activities such as bidding for construction projects, transfer of profit-making land use rights, and real estate development and operation.

Any violation of this Article shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 97 of the Regulations on Sanctions for Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 18. Personnel of the people's courts who violate these Provisions but can promptly and voluntarily correct their actions may be dealt with leniently. If the circumstances are relatively minor, a sanction may be waived, but criticism and education shall be given; if the circumstances are relatively serious, a lighter or mitigated sanction may be imposed, and where necessary, corresponding organizational measures may also be taken.

If personnel of the people's courts violate these Provisions and need to receive administrative sanctions or are suspected of committing crimes, the matter shall be transferred to the relevant authorities in accordance with the law.

Article 19. Economic benefits obtained by personnel of the people's courts through violation of these Provisions shall be confiscated; other benefits obtained through violation of these Provisions shall be corrected or revoked in accordance with the law or relevant regulations.

Article 20. The term "personnel of the people's courts" as used in these Provisions refers to personnel within the administrative staffing and institutional staffing of the people's courts at all levels.

The term "leading cadres of the people's courts" as used in these Provisions refers to members of the leadership bodies and full-time members of the Adjudication Committees of the people's courts at all levels.

The term "judges serving in adjudication and enforcement positions" as used in these Provisions refers to members of the Adjudication Committees who do not hold leadership positions at the court level, as well as judges and enforcement officers engaged in adjudication and enforcement work in departments such as case filing, adjudication, enforcement, adjudication supervision, and state compensation at the people's courts at all levels.

The term "personnel in comprehensive administrative positions" as used in these Provisions refers to personnel of the people's courts who are engaged in comprehensive administrative management and judicial auxiliary work in the internal departments of the people's courts at all levels.

Article 21. The term "other persons with whom they have a special relationship" as used in these Provisions refers to persons other than the spouses, children, and children's spouses of personnel of the people's courts who are close relatives or have a close relationship.

Article 22. If any previously issued provisions of the Supreme People's Court are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.

Article 23. The interpretation of these Provisions shall be the responsibility of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 24. These Provisions shall come into effect on the date of issuance.
